suggestion: Decide the price-data policy in writing before another week of capture.
why: Every blocked requirement in this desk traces to one of two missing things: an official price, or permission to store one. Capturing a 15th week of injuries does not move either.
unblocks: R01, R02, R60, R71 and every reward tier
adopt_path: Write the policy line into the repo; name the source or state that none is permitted; then build the price store against it.
defer_path: Keep capturing availability only; publish no price-dependent number.
reject_path: Continue without a policy and accept that no backtest can ever be scored, which makes the leaderboard unscoreable by construction.

suggestion: Schedule the capture instead of doing it by hand: every Game Book within 24 hours of kickoff, and the injury report three times a week.
why: This desk closed Week 10 by hand on 2026-11-18, two days after the last game. A scheduled job would have done it the same night, and would already hold the Wednesday Week 11 capture that does not exist today.
cost: one scheduled job plus immutable storage outside the static site
adopt_path: Stand up the job against the same parsers this repo already has; store raw captures with hashes off-site; alert on schema change.
defer_path: Keep manual capture and accept that every week is two days stale.
reject_path: Do not capture on a schedule and the point-in-time ledger stays a single snapshot, which cannot support a backtest.

suggestion: Take the snapshot before kickoff, always, and stamp it with kickoff time.
why: Found today: the NFL injury report re-renders club records after the game (0-8 became 1-8 on identical player rows). A post-kickoff capture is contaminated by the result and would leak into any backtest.
cost: a kickoff field and a hard rule in the capture job
adopt_path: Refuse any capture whose timestamp is at or after kickoff; keep the record field out of every feature.
defer_path: Capture whenever convenient and mark the affected weeks unusable.
reject_path: Allow post-kickoff captures and every personnel backtest becomes lookahead-contaminated.

suggestion: Publish the reserve-list gap as a standing number, not a footnote.
why: 86 of 158 Week 10 inactives (0.5443) never appear on the injury report. Any model that reads 'no row' as 'available' is wrong more often than it is right.
cost: one field in the daily capture
unblocks: R64 and every personnel feature built on the report
adopt_path: Join official transactions and reserve lists daily; treat absence as unknown, never as healthy.
defer_path: Keep the report-only view and label personnel features as partial.
reject_path: Assume absence means available, and the availability graph is wrong.

suggestion: Resolve the snap-count source question once, in writing, then stop asking.
why: Four probes today found no official snap counts on team stats, player stats, the Game Book, or 13 retained Game Book extracts. Re-litigating this each session costs time and changes nothing.
cost: one line in the method page plus a standing probe
unblocks: R11, R31, R56 (all three stay open either way)
adopt_path: Record 'no official snap source found, re-probe each season'; use the Game Book starter list as the official playing-participation proxy.
reject_path: Derive depth from jersey number, experience or salary - already rejected in the brief, and rejected here again.

suggestion: Archive past-season weekly injury reports before promising a calibration.
why: Questionable now has n=18 and an interval from 0.1270 to 0.5104. That is a measurement, not a calibration, and no amount of current-season data fixes it.
cost: an archive job for at least two prior seasons
adopt_path: Archive weekly reports season by season; only then join designations to inactive lists and publish a rate per designation.
defer_path: Publish the current interval with its width on every page that uses it.
reject_path: Use legacy percentages such as 'Questionable means 50%'; nothing in the official text supports any number.

suggestion: Keep the site split: public analysis on the site, raw rows in a private store, until the terms are read.
why: The official Game Book carries an explicit copyright notice restricting use to media coverage without written permission. Publishing derived analysis with links is defensible; republishing row-level data is not yet assessed.
adopt_path: Keep raw captures in a private store; publish aggregates and links only.
defer_path: Publish nothing row-level, as this desk does today.
reject_path: Republish raw rows on the public site before the terms are read.

suggestion: Add a control baseline and a pre-registration commit before any strategy is allowed onto the leaderboard.
why: A leaderboard with no random-pick and favourites-only control cannot separate skill from a favourable week, and a strategy defined after seeing results is not a strategy.
cost: two rows in the leaderboard builder and one commit per strategy
unblocks: R67, R73, R74 and the demotion gate
adopt_path: Freeze the rule text, sample window and gates in a commit before the evaluation window opens; publish controls beside every ranking.
defer_path: Publish no ranking at all, which is what the competition desk does.
reject_path: Rank on realised ROI alone - explicitly rejected in the brief.
